solutionSteps: [1 mark] (a) Lower pH means more acidic; the lowest pH is 2, so solution A is the most acidic.
[1 mark] (b) Higher pH means more basic; the highest pH is 12, so solution C is the most basic.
[1 mark] (c) pH 7 is neutral, so solution B is neutral.
[1 mark] (d) Hydrogen ion concentration increases as pH decreases: C (12) < E (9) < B (7) < D (5) < A (2).
fields.finalAnswer: (a) A (b) C (c) B (d) C < E < B < D < A

fields.questionText: Four samples of hydrochloric acid, each of volume 100 mL, have different pH values. Which sample would require the least amount of base to neutralise it completely?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] For the same volume (100 mL), a higher pH means a lower H⁺ ion concentration, so less base is needed to neutralise it; the HCl solution of pH 4 has the highest pH and therefore needs the least base.
fields.explanation: The amount of base needed depends on how many H⁺ ions the acid contains. For equal volumes, a higher pH means a lower H⁺ ion concentration. The pH 4 sample has the fewest H⁺ ions, so it needs the least base. Therefore, the correct answer is B) HCl solution of pH 4.
